response.title: Should I avoid older power stations with the regular lithium battery and only buy the newer long-life kind?
response.answer:
Yes. For most people buying a portable power station today, I recommend choosing the newer LiFePO4 (LFP) battery technology instead of the older lithium-ion (NMC) technology.

But I wouldn't completely rule out older models, especially if they're heavily discounted or you need something lightweight.

The difference is significant enough that battery chemistry should be one of your main purchasing considerations.

LiFePO4 vs. older lithium-ion power stations

Feature

	

Older lithium-ion (NMC)

	

Newer LiFePO4 (LFP)




Typical cycle life

	

500–1,000 cycles

	

2,500–4,000+ cycles




Safety

	

Good with proper protection

	

Better thermal stability




Weight

	

Lighter

	

Heavier




Energy density

	

Higher

	

Lower




Long-term durability

	

Moderate

	

Excellent




Best use

	

Occasional use, portable applications

	

Regular use, home backup, long-term ownership

Cycle life figures are approximate. Manufacturers often define cycle life as the number of full-equivalent cycles until the battery retains around 80% of its original capacity.

Why I generally prefer LiFePO4

1. Much longer lifespan. An LFP power station rated for 3,000 cycles could theoretically withstand one full charge-discharge cycle every day for more than eight years before reaching its specified capacity threshold. That doesn't mean the entire power station is guaranteed to last eight years, but it's a major advantage.

2. Better thermal stability. LFP cells are generally less prone to thermal runaway than NMC cells. Both still require good battery management systems, temperature protection, and proper charging.

3. Better value over time. Even if an LFP model costs slightly more, its longer cycle life can make it cheaper over years of regular use.

When would I still buy an older lithium-ion model?

For a new purchase, my rule of thumb would be:

Same price: Definitely choose LFP.

Older NMC model 20% cheaper: I'd still lean toward LFP.

Older NMC model 40–50% cheaper: Worth considering for occasional use.

Buying used: I'd strongly favor LFP, unless the older unit's battery health is verifiable.

These discounts are my suggested decision thresholds, not universal rules.

One important distinction: LFP is also a lithium-ion battery. A product labeled simply "lithium-ion" isn't necessarily using the older chemistry. Check its specifications.

Also, cycle life isn't everything. Batteries age with time even when rarely used, and power station electronics can fail before the battery wears out. 
USAID
+1

One question that could change my recommendation
Emergency backup — a few times per year
Camping and occasional outdoor use
Regular use — weekly or daily
Solar charging or off-grid use
Get recommendation for my usage

For emergency-only use, the economics are quite different from daily use, because you may never get close to the rated cycle limit of either battery.
